newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean president orders probe into Hanbo scandal.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean president orders probe into Hanbo scandal.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam on Monday ordered a probe into the Hanbo Group after opposition parties alleged government complicity in what they called irregular loans to its failed steel unit.
Opposition parties issued a joint statement calling the loans to Hanbo Steel Co the biggest financial scandal in the country's history.
"In a meeting with Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung, President Kim ordered the government to carry out a thorough investigation into the Hanbo Group," Kim's spokesman said.
Hanbo Steel, the group's flagship, has defaulted on debt and is seeking court protection with three other group units.
Later, Kim's ruling party bowed to opposition demands for a parliamentary probe into the financial affairs of the country's 14th largest industrial conglomerate.
The New Korea Party agreed to the investigation on condition it did not hamper a separate probe by state prosecutors, a party statement said.

The main opposition National Congress for New Politics and United Liberal Democratic Party said a parliamentary probe was needed because of suspicions the government supported loans to Hanbo despite its shaky financial status.
"The Hanbo incident is the biggest ever power-linked financial irregularity," their statement said, adding it had "dealt a fatal shock" to the economy.
Finance ministry officials say Hanbo borrowed about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) from banks and financial institutions against its net worth of 224.3 billion won.
The ruling party statement accused the opposition of spreading "unfounded rumours" about the Hanbo Group and said the probe must involve the opposition as well as the ruling camp.
It said prosecutors should first carry out a thorough government-level investigation but the ruling party also agreed to open a separate parliamentary probe.
Analysts fear Hanbo's failure could spark a chain reaction of corporate bankruptcies and threaten banks who have lent to the country's second biggest steel maker without securing adequate collateral.
Hanbo Steel's problems stem from huge plant expansion in the southern city of Tangjin.
The Justice Ministry has banned Hanbo's top executives, including founder Chung Tae-soo, from leaving the country. ($=845.70)
